summary: The UK's Commonwealth Scholarship Commission funds PhDs at UK universities for citizens of the Commonwealth's least developed and most fragile countries, among them Nigeria, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Uganda and Zambia. It pays full tuition, a stipend of £1,712 a month (£2,000 in London) for 36 months, flights and other allowances. You apply through a nominator in your country, not to the Commission. The 2027–28 round closed on 20 October 2026.
meta_title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships: who can apply and the next round
meta_description: UK PhD funding for citizens of 17 Commonwealth countries including Nigeria: full fees, £1,712 a month, flights. How nomination works and when it opens.
covers: Full tuition fees, by agreement between the Commission and the UK university.
A stipend of £1,712 a month, or £2,000 a month at London universities.
Approved airfare to and from the UK, a study travel grant, fieldwork airfare, a paid mid-term visit home and family allowances.
eligibility: Citizens of, or refugees in, an eligible country who live there permanently: Bangladesh, The Gambia, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, Pakistan, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Togo, Tuvalu, Uganda and Zambia.
A first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours, or a lower second plus a relevant postgraduate qualification.
No age limit. For a 2027 start you must not have registered for a PhD before September or October 2026.
Ghana and Kenya are not on the list.
how_to_apply: Apply to a nominator, usually your country's national nominating agency or a selected NGO; the Commission does not accept direct applications.
Complete the application in CSC Central, the Commission's online portal.
Nominators put candidates forward to the Commission in December.
The 2027–28 deadline was 16:00 BST on 20 October 2026; watch for the 2028–29 call.
watch_out: Nominating agencies set their own, earlier deadlines.
Split-site PhD Scholarships for low and middle income countries are paused for 2026 and 2027.
Funding covers 36 months of full-time study only.
Ghana and Kenya are not eligible for this PhD scheme; their citizens can look at the Commonwealth Master's Scholarships.
costs: Paid in full by agreement between the Commission and the university
A stipend of £1,712 a month (£2,000 in London)
Flights to and from the UK
documents: Your nominator's own application and documents
Degree certificates and transcripts showing a 2:1, or a 2:2 with a relevant postgraduate qualification

faq.q: Can Ghanaians apply for the Commonwealth PhD Scholarship?
faq.a: No. Ghana is not on the list of eligible countries for the PhD scheme. Nigeria, Uganda, Zambia, Malawi and Rwanda are among the African countries that are.
Through a nominator in your country, such as the national nominating agency, using the CSC Central portal. The Commission does not take direct applications.
The 2027–28 round closed on 20 October 2026. The 2028–29 round is not yet announced.
